text:
The biggest story around the Rangers this month is in the crease. They placed James Reimer on unconditional waivers to terminate his contract (Sportsnet), which left Dylan Garand carrying the load, and Joonas Korpisalo won his season debut in Seattle on Saturday. Igor Shesterkin's last four starts were excellent (.926, 4.0 goals saved above expected), but he wasn't one of the two goalies in the lineup the New York Post's Mollie Walker posted for Monday's game in Edmonton. Who's in net over the next couple of weeks is the thing to watch.

The skaters have earned more than 10-8-1 suggests. The Rangers take 53.5 percent of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) and 53 percent at five on five, and they've scored 8.25 fewer goals than their chances deserve. Monday was the season in miniature: 60 shot attempts to 40, a 3-1 loss to Devon Levi.

Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault have 58 percent of the expected goals together. J.T. Miller, Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye are at 60 percent but have been outscored 4-7, the kind of gap that tends to close. Kartye has been the pleasant surprise; Sports Illustrated called him "Emerging as Building Block for NY Rangers." Our simulations give Mike Sullivan's team a 53 percent playoff chance. If the finishing comes around, that's the low end.
headline: The goalie question behind a better-than-it-looks team
